Responsibilities

The Device Characterization Engineering Intern will support semiconductor device characterization and yield improvement activities within a high-volume manufacturing environment. The intern will work alongside Device, Integration, Probe/Test, and Process Engineering teams to analyze electrical test data, identify device and process-related performance trends, and develop data-driven approaches to improve product yield and manufacturing performance.

The role provides hands-on exposure to semiconductor device behavior, electrical characterization, wafer-level test data, statistical analysis, and structured problem solving.

Responsibilities

- Analyze wafer-level electrical and probe test data to identify yield trends, outliers, and systematic performance signatures.

- Perform data mining and statistical analysis to correlate electrical characteristics with process, device, and manufacturing variables.

- Support characterization of semiconductor devices across operating conditions and manufacturing variation.

- Investigate electrical parameters and device performance distributions to identify opportunities for yield improvement.

- Develop analytical models, visualizations, or automated methods to improve detection and understanding of device and yield trends.

- Work with Device, Integration, Probe/Test, and Process Engineering teams to investigate manufacturing and product performance issues.

- Apply structured problem-solving methods to identify potential drivers of electrical performance variation.

- Summarize technical findings and communicate conclusions and recommendations to engineering teams.

- Complete an internship project with a defined technical deliverable demonstrating measurable improvement or new insight into device/yield performance.

Qualifications

Qualifications – External

Required

- Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering

- Junior or senior undergraduate standing preferred.

- Coursework or fundamental understanding of semiconductor devices and basic electrical characteristics.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

- Experience analyzing technical or quantitative data.

- Ability to communicate technical results clearly and work effectively across engineering disciplines.

Preferred

- Familiarity with MOSFETs, semiconductor device physics, or electrical characterization.

- Exposure to statistical analysis, semiconductor manufacturing, wafer probe/test, or yield engineering.

- Experience with Python, MATLAB, JMP, Excel, or similar data-analysis tools.

- Familiarity with data visualization, statistical modeling, or machine-learning techniques.

At Toyota Research Institute (TRI), we’re on a mission to improve the quality of human life. We’re developing new tools and capabilities to amplify the human experience. To lead this transformative shift in mobility, we’ve built a world-class team advancing the state of the art in AI, robotics, driving, and material sciences.

This is a paid 12-week internship opportunity and is a hybrid, in-office role.

Here’s a glimpse into the Internship experience from some of our TRI interns!

The Team

Within the Extreme Performance Intelligent Control team, we are developing techniques to advance vehicle safety and performance capabilities using tools from machine learning, optimization, and control theory. We pursue a hybrid approach to high-performance driving that unites physics-based optimal control with data-driven learning. By embedding vehicle dynamics and optimization structure into learned controllers, we aim to build systems that adapt to uncertainty and match or exceed expert drivers while retaining the interpretability and guarantees of classical methods.

The Internship

We are seeking a motivated intern to join our team, focusing on cutting-edge research combining machine learning with physical system knowledge and control theory to develop reliable controllers for autonomous vehicles. Potential research areas include designing learning-based control methods that enforce forward invariance, stability, and constraint satisfaction; and incorporating vehicle dynamics and other physical knowledge into learning and control amid challenging driving scenarios.

This role provides an exciting opportunity to explore approaches to machine learning for control that support safe, intuitive, and responsive driving systems. Along the way you will apply your knowledge to tackle novel research questions and work towards a publication with professional researchers. The internship will be in our headquarters in Los Altos, CA and includes competitive compensation befitting the challenging, but fun, nature of the research work at TRI. Applicants with relevant publications in the fields above and good collaboration skills are highly encouraged to apply.

Responsibilities

- Work with researchers to develop and then undertake a well-scoped research project in a relevant area.

- Extend existing controls/AI/ML algorithms or design new algorithms for control at a vehicle’s performance limit.

- Explore approaches to formalize guarantees of safety for machine learning algorithms.

- Implement algorithms on a full scale vehicle research platform.

- Publish your original research at a high impact conference.

Qualifications

- Ph.D. or M.S. student in relevant fields - ML/AI, robotics, computer science, mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or similar.

- Proficient in scientific Python, Unix, and robotic frameworks (e.g. ROS2.0).

- Knowledge of machine learning, nonlinear system control, and optimal control. Vehicle dynamics knowledge is a plus.

- Experience working on joint scientific and engineering projects.

- Familiarity with or interest in racing or high-performance driving is a plus.

At REGENT, we’re on a mission to revolutionize regional transportation between coastal cities. We're not just building vehicles, we're creating a new category of transportation: the Seaglider. These groundbreaking wing-in-ground-effect craft travel just above the water’s surface, combining the speed of an airplane with the low operating costs of a boat. Capable of 180 miles at 180 mph on today's battery tech (and up to 400 miles with next-gen batteries), Seagliders will unlock fast, affordable, and sustainable coastal transit for passengers and cargo - connecting cities, islands, and communities like never before.

Backed by leading investors and powered by a team of passionate, forward-thinking engineers, builders, and operators, we’re now scaling from a breakthrough prototype to full production - and building the team to make it happen.

Role Overview

REGENT's Mass Properties discipline sits at the heart of every vehicle program. As the Mass Properties Engineering Intern, you'll work directly on real, high-impact work from day one.

This isn't spreadsheet upkeep. You'll do the engineering a full-time hire would do: pulling mass, CG, and inertia data directly from CAD, working with various IPTs to keep the data accurate, and writing scripts that replace manual work. You'll help close out weight and balance control for our prototype vehicle, and help define the management plan, database architecture, and tools that our production craft will rely on through production.

You'll join the Aero & Performance team within Hardware Engineering. If you'd rather open a CAD model and find the answer yourself, write a script than repeat a task by hand, and help build a discipline instead of plugging into one that already exists, you'll fit right in!

What You'll Do

- Support R&D W&B Control: You'll help develop and implement the processes that control our products’ weight and balance properties through the maturation of design, including how mass data is sourced, verified, updated through configuration changes, and reported.

- Build Supporting Tools: You'll write scripts to automate reporting of mass properties and mass rollups across programs, establishing the appropriate checks and balances.

- Work Laterally Across the Company: You'll gain a system view by interfacing directly with adjacent departments (structures, propulsion, avionics, etc) to collect mass properties, challenge their reports, and keep the database up to date.

- Exposure to Design Tools: You'll have visibility into the PLM system and the DMU to gain a deeper understanding of the system layout and reports generated by the responsible engineers.

- Identify Risks and Opportunities: You'll assess mass and balance data to flag potential weight or CG issues, identify opportunities to reduce weight, and share your findings with the relevant engineering teams.

- Define and Deliver a Real Outcome: You'll scope a clear goal with your manager early in the term and present your results, including your assumptions and data sources, to the team at the end of it.

- Set Your Priorities: You'll work independently under the guidance of the Mass Properties Engineer, who will mentor you and help you define your priorities across the different programs to achieve your set objectives.

What You'll Bring

- CAD Fluency: You can navigate CATIA, SolidWorks, NX or similar tools to independently understand the vehicle layout, pull mass, CG, and inertia data.

- Scripting Instincts: You have working proficiency in Python, MATLAB, SQL, VBA, or similar, and you reach for a script when a task is about to become a recurring manual chore.

- Weight and Balance Fundamentals: You understand CG calculations, moment of inertia, and how margins and contingencies get carried through a program.

- Comfort With Ambiguity: You are able to focus across multiple active programs and changing priorities.

- Confidence Reaching Out: You are proactive and comfortable engaging with engineers on other teams directly to track down a number and get it confirmed.

- Curiosity About Change Control: Exposure to PLM or PDM systems and interest in how engineering changes are tracked through the lifecycle of a program is an advantage.

- A Head Start, If You've Got One: Though we don't expect you to have it, familiarity with aircraft weight management standards, having a private pilot’s license, or prior weight and balance experience from a program, class, or club project, will help you ramp up quickly.

Who We're Looking For

- Collaborative Team Player: You believe that great things happen when teams work together. You communicate effectively and collaborate with engineers, stakeholders, and other cross-functional teams to align on goals and move projects forward. You bring people together, ensuring that everyone is on the same page and moving towards a shared vision.

- Creative Problem Solver: You thrive on tackling complex challenges and finding innovative solutions. Whether you're resolving installation challenges, debugging elusive electrical issues, or adapting on the fly during integration and test, you bring a practical, inventive mindset to every problem. You don't just patch issues - you improve processes, anticipate downstream impacts, and help turn one-off fixes into scalable solutions that raise the bar for future builds.

- Adaptable & Agile: In a fast-paced, ever-evolving startup environment, you quickly adapt to changing priorities and requirements. You approach challenges with a calm, resilient mindset, and know how to pivot and adjust your approach as needed, ensuring that progress continues without missing a beat.

- Innovative Mindset: You’re driven by curiosity and a passion for technology. You’re passionate about driving continuous improvement, embracing new technologies and methodologies to enhance efficiency, quality, and team performance.

- Housing Stipend available for those temporarily moving to join our team

We value diverse skillsets and experiences and believe in the potential of passionate individuals to make a big impact.

SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. AI at SharkNinja

At SharkNinja, we’re building an AI-native culture. We’re not waiting for the future; we’re creating it. Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. If you believe the best way to do your job hasn’t been invented yet, you’ll fit right in.

Join the SharkNinja Early Edge Experience: Built for early career talent. Geared toward impact. Driven by speed. Whether you’re in a co-op or internship, our early talent program is designed to provide valuable exposure to the industry and a fast-paced professional environment. Along the way, you’ll benefit from professional development opportunities, community events, and connections that make your experience well-rounded and enriching. Are you excited by the challenge of building — and breaking — the next generation of high-performance consumer products? If so, we invite you to learn more about the Engineering & Technology Co-op at SharkNinja.

This is a single application for engineering and technology early talent opportunities across SharkNinja. The hiring teams are spread across our electrical, embedded, software, robotics, digital, quality, test, and safety functions.

Whichever team you join, you’ll work alongside experienced engineers on products that reach millions of homes. You might be bringing up a new circuit board, tuning a control algorithm on a robot, writing cloud or mobile code for a connected appliance, building a test rig that runs thousands of cycles, investigating a field return, or helping keep our products and facilities safe and compliant. If you’re technically curious, hands-on, solution-oriented, and ready to make an impact from day one, we want to hear from you!

- Electrical Engineering (Shark and Ninja)

- Electrical Design Engineering, Advanced Development

- Firmware & Embedded Software Engineering

- Control Systems & Algorithms

- Robotics & Mechatronics

- Software Engineering

- Web Development (CodeShark)

- Mobile App Development

- Software & Technical Program Management

- Digital & Website Technology

- IT Service Desk

- Product Test Engineering

- Software Quality Assurance & Test Automation

- System Quality Assurance (Robotics)

- CORE Quality (Consumer, Operational, Regulatory & Engineering)

- Product Safety & Regulatory Compliance

- Environmental Health & Safety (EHS)

- Contribute to the design, development, and validation of next-generation Shark and Ninja products — and the software that powers them

- Work hands-on in labs, at the bench, and in code: building prototypes, test fixtures, scripts, and tools that engineers actually use

- Support debugging, troubleshooting, root cause analysis, and failure investigation on real products and real consumer data

- Develop and execute test plans, document results, and turn data into recommendations that shape design decisions

- Participate in design reviews, sprints, stand-ups, and technical discussions alongside experienced engineers

- Collaborate cross-functionally with Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Design, Firmware, Quality, Operations, Marketing, and Product Management

- Gain exposure to the full product development lifecycle — ideation and prototyping through certification, mass production readiness, and post-market consumer feedback

- Own a meaningful project end to end and present your contributions to SharkNinja leaders

- Board bring-up, debugging, and validation of real-time embedded electronics, including serial communication protocols such as I2C, SPI, and UART

- Writing and debugging firmware in C/C++ for microcontrollers and prototyping on platforms such as Arduino or Raspberry Pi

- Developing classical (e.g., PID) and advanced (e.g., MPC) control algorithms in Python, MATLAB, or C++ and tuning them on real hardware

- Working with robotics and navigation technologies such as LiDAR, Time-of-Flight sensors, and SLAM/V-SLAM

- Supporting EMC, safety, and certification testing, EBOM/CBOM cost analysis, DVT, and DFMEA

Software, Digital & IT

- Developing cross-platform mobile apps in React Native, TypeScript, Swift, Kotlin, or Rust that communicate with devices over BLE, Wi-Fi, MQTT, and RESTful APIs

Quality, Test, Safety & Compliance

- Writing automated test scripts in Python or C++ and integrating sensors, microcontrollers, and data acquisition tools into test setups

- Executing manual and system-level test protocols for products, robots, and mobile apps, and documenting defects in JIRA or similar tools

- Tearing down SharkNinja and competitor products, analyzing large data sets with statistical tools, and investigating failure modes

- Evaluating consumer field returns, star reviews, and call center feedback to drive root cause analysis and corrective actions

- Supporting product safety and regulatory compliance work, internal audits, risk assessments, EHS inspections, and safety training aligned to standards such as OSHA and EPA

- Programming or scripting experience in one or more of C, C++, Python, MATLAB, TypeScript, JavaScript, Java, Kotlin, or Swift

- Able to read and interpret schematics, technical drawings, and product requirements

- A natural communicator who can explain complex technical topics clearly to both technical and non-technical stakeholders, in writing and out loud

- Strong attention to detail in testing, documentation, and data analysis; offers data-backed insights and constructive feedback

- Comfortable multitasking and shifting between immediate tasks and longer-term projects in a fast-paced environment, with proactive ownership of your work
